transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Tom Alvarez (Redwood); Priya Kapoor, Ethan Ross, Laura Kim (AuroraSearch)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Tom, our solutions engineer. We'll walk through hosted embeddings and the rerank endpoint and show how the Console + Optimize suggestions help tune cost/latency.
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: Thanks, Maya. Quick context: we run search for e-commerce catalog, about 12M SKUs, current infra is Elasticsearch for text search + Pinecone for vectors, looking to improve relevance for long-tail queries and speed up rerank.
[00:40] Tom Alvarez: Got it. We'll start with the integration pattern: you call Redwood embeddings endpoint to vectorize docs and queries, store vectors in your vector DB (we work with Pinecone, Weaviate, FAISS, etc), then call our rerank endpoint with top-k candidates to get relevance scores.
[01:05] Ethan Ross: So the rerank endpoint returns a score only? Or a full LLM output? Concerned about token costs.
[01:13] Tom Alvarez: Good question. Rerank returns a compact JSON with scores and optional explainability fields. It's optimized for short context so token usage is low. There's a streaming option if you want detailed explain text, but most customers use the compact scores.
[01:30] Laura Kim: How do we handle embeddings at scale? We have nightly updates and about 10k new docs per day.
[01:38] Tom Alvarez: We support bulk batch embeddings. Two patterns: incremental batch with our bulk endpoint, or embed at ingest time. We also have Optimize suggestions in Console that recommend batching sizes, concurrency, and quantization settings if you want to reduce memory and cost.
[02:00] Priya Kapoor: You mentioned quant — quantization? Any drop in quality?
[02:05] Tom Alvarez: We recommend int8 or q4_x4 for production inference on embeddings; It's model-dependent. Optimize's recommendations are workload-aware — it will flag quality regressions against your eval set. There can be small differences but usually within acceptable thresholds for search rerank.
[02:30] Maya Chen: I'll show a short live demo of the API flow and then Tom will jump into Console and Optimize.

[03:10] Tom Alvarez: (screen share) Here is the API docs: POST /v1/embeddings, sample payload, returns 768-dim vectors for the model we picked. Then we do a top-k retrieval from your vector DB and send top 50 candidates to POST /v1/rerank with the query + small context.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: Top 50 seems high — what's the latency impact?
[03:52] Tom Alvarez: Typical rerank latency for 50 items is 120-230ms in Hosted for our default model, depends on seq length and prompt. If latency needs to be <100ms we recommend either a smaller k or a lighter rerank model and we can do A/B test with Optimize to measure quality impact.
[04:20] Ethan Ross: Are there built-in caching options? We have repeated queries.
[04:26] Tom Alvarez: Yes, we have prefix/K-V cache — uh, K-V cash in some exports — it caches key vector contexts to avoid recomputation. Console shows cache hit rates and you can configure TTL. That reduces per-query cost dramatically for repeated queries.
[04:50] Laura Kim: How do we store keys securely? We have strict compliance, must use customer-managed keys.
[04:55] Maya Chen: For Hosted we integrate with KM-s integrations, sorry KMS — customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. We also provide audit logs and SOC 2 Type II reports. If you need VPC peering or Private (on-prem) we can do that as well.
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: Good. For data residency, some EU customers need EU-only. Is that supported?
[05:27] Tom Alvarez: Yes, region pinning is supported and we can set a European-only tenant for data storage.

[06:00] Tom Alvarez: I'll run a quick demo rerank example. (types) Query: ‘waterproof hiking boots size 10 women’ — I send embeddings, retrieve top 100 from vector DB, then post top 30 to rerank. You can see scores returned, and we provide normalized relevance.
[06:35] Priya Kapoor: The numbers look good, but curious about cost. Can you show cost per 1k reranks?
[06:42] Maya Chen: Sure, rough hosted numbers: embeddings cost depends on model and dims; rerank is priced per call and per token for optional explain. For a compact rerank (scores only) it's about $0.0008 per call at these volumes; Optimize can suggest batching and caching to cut cost 3x in many workloads.
[07:10] Ethan Ross: Are there concurrency limits? Our peak qps is 400.
[07:15] Tom Alvarez: Hosted has soft rate limits; for sustained 400 QPS we recommend Dedicated or reserved capacity. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and autoscaling. We can simulate load in POC to estimate capacity needed.

[08:00] Laura Kim: Integration effort—how long to get endpoint working?
[08:05] Maya Chen: Self-serve can be minutes to a day. For POC with benchmarks and production advice, typical timeline is 2-4 weeks including security review.

[09:12] (minor crosstalk)
[09:30] Tom Alvarez: Switching to Console: here's the model catalog page, latency profiles, per-route dashboards. Optimize tab shows batching recommendations, suggested quant profiles, and historical quality vs cost charts keyed by your eval prompts. You can import your eval set and we run continuous regression checks.
[10:05] Priya Kapoor: Does Optimize change model selection automatically?
[10:10] Tom Alvarez: No auto-switch by default; it will surface candidate model variants and you can opt into canary rollouts. We also have automatic fallback policies if primary capacity is constrained.

[11:00] Priya Kapoor: Security follow-ups: do you support SAML SSO, RBAC, org-level audit logs?
[11:08] Maya Chen: Yes, SSO via SAML/OAuth, granular RBAC, org-wide audit logs available. We'll share the security whitepaper and compliance pack.

[12:00] Ethan Ross: Any examples of rerank templates? We want to maintain interpretability for business users.
[12:07] Tom Alvarez: We'll send a notebook with prompted templates (we have a few: pairwise scoring, listwise scoring, and hybrid prompt that uses product attributes). We'll include suggested prompt engineering for categories and synonyms.

[14:00] Priya Kapoor: How are vector updates handled during product updates — do you re-embed everything?
[14:07] Tom Alvarez: Common pattern: re-embed changed docs only. We provide incremental bulk endpoints and we can do streaming uploads. Also Console shows embedding drift metrics so you know when model re-embed is recommended.

[16:20] Laura Kim: For the POC, we want to run a benchmark with 100k docs, compare current Pinecone pipeline vs Redwood + same vector DB. Can you support that?
[16:28] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Tom will prepare a benchmark script. We'll need a sample dataset and your success criteria (latency, recall@10, conversion proxy).

[18:00] (brief pause, audio fuzz)
[18:15] Priya Kapoor: Quick question on SLA if we move to Dedicated.
[18:20] Maya Chen: Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs for a committed capacity plan. We'll include SLA language in the pricing packet.

[20:00] Tom Alvarez: Back to rerank architecture: we also support hybrid rerank where we append product metadata (price, availability) into the prompt so the model can prefer in-stock items — only include minimal fields to keep tokens low.
[20:32] Ethan Ross: That helps. Any monitoring hooks?
[20:36] Tom Alvarez: We export traces and per-request token breakdowns, cost attribution by route/token, and you can hook tracing to your existing APM.

[22:00] Priya Kapoor: Any gotchas?
[22:05] Tom Alvarez: Watch out for prompt length — longer candidate contexts increase tokens and latency. Also embedding dimension changes across models; if you switch models you may need to reindex. Optimize flags that.

[25:00] Laura Kim: Will Redwood manage vector DB if we want fully managed?
[25:06] Maya Chen: We don't currently host vector DBs ourselves — we integrate with partner managed options. For Dedicated we can run co-located vector stores in customer VPC for tighter integration.

[27:30] (customer small talk about holiday roadmap)

[29:00] Tom Alvarez: Demo wrap: I'm going to run a live latency test against our hosted rerank with a lower-k example (k=10) to show <100ms 95th p99 numbers for this model. (shares a chart) You can see median ~55ms, p95 ~94ms.
[29:40] Priya Kapoor: That looks promising. What about cost when you scale to millions of queries per day?
[29:46] Maya Chen: At scale, Dedicated and batching/caching dramatically reduce unit cost. We'll run cost-modeling in the POC.

[32:00] (discussion on fallback policies and A/B rollouts)
[34:00] Priya Kapoor: Who are our contacts for contract/security?
[34:05] Maya Chen: I'll be primary AE contact. For technical, Tom is the SE. For security docs, I'll route you to our trust team and share the pack.

[36:00] Ethan Ross: Do you have any published benchmarks for embed+rerank against open models?
[36:07] Tom Alvarez: Yes, we have a benchmark repo and tuned profiles in Console. I'll share the link — note sometimes model names in the doc are abbreviated, e.g., ‘rwd-embed-xl’ in the catalog.

[38:00] (small overlap)
[38:20] Priya Kapoor: Ok let's recap and confirm next steps.
[38:25] Maya Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood will send pricing + SLA details; 2) Tom will prepare benchmark script and sample dataset; 3) AuroraSearch to confirm success criteria and any residency/KMS constraints; 4) Schedule POC kickoff for next week.
[38:50] Laura Kim: Sounds good — we'll aim to confirm criteria by Friday.

[40:00] (end of demo flow, some attendees drop video)
[41:10] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff and attach the security whitepaper and example Notebooks.
[41:30] Priya Kapoor: Thanks, everyone. Excited to see the POC run.

[42:00] (call closing chatter, thanks)

Meeting artifacts referenced:
- Quickstart Notebook (link: https://redwood.example.com/quickstart/aurorasearch-notebook)
- Pricing PDF (shared after call)
- Security whitepaper & SOC2 report (will be shared via secure link)
